Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

meta

Declare generic effect sizes and sampling variances

Stata 

meta set yi sei

R metafor 

metafor::escalc(measure = "GEN", yi = yi, sei = sei, data = data)

Differs from Stata Both examples take standard errors as sei; metafor stores their squares as vi. escalc creates effect-size data but does not persist a Stata-style meta declaration, labels or a default analysis model.

Stata reference · R reference

Cumulative fixed-effect meta-analysis by year

Stata 

meta summarize, cumulative(year)

R metafor 

metafor::cumul(metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = data, method = "REML"), order = data$year)

Differs from Stata Assumes meta set used its default random(reml) declaration; metafor explicitly selects REML. A prior Stata common/fixed/random declaration changes the target. Match study order, missingness and heterogeneity estimation before comparing summaries.

Stata reference · R reference

Inverse-variance meta-analysis using FE

Stata 

meta summarize, fixed

R metafor 

metafor::rma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = data, method = "FE")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Between-study variance estimators and confidence procedures must be matched; some R estimator names differ from Stata's names.

23 more examples and alternatives

Rank-correlation small-study-effects test

Stata 

meta bias, begg

R metafor 

metafor::ranktest(metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = data, method = "FE"))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Rank-correlation and small-sample p-value conventions may differ.

Stata reference · R reference

Egger regression asymmetry test

Stata 

meta bias, egger

R metafor 

metafor::regtest(metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = data, method = "REML"), model = "rma", predictor = "sei")

Differs from Stata Assumes the Stata meta declaration is its default random(reml). model="rma" regresses the effects on their standard errors with additive REML heterogeneity; model="lm" would instead use multiplicative dispersion. Small-study effects alone do not establish publication bias.

Stata reference · R reference

Freeman-Tukey transformed proportions

Stata 

meta esize cases n, esize(ftukeyprop)

R metafor 

{ out <- metafor::escalc(measure = "PFT", xi = cases, ni = n, data = data); out$yi <- 2 * out$yi; out$vi <- 4 * out$vi; out }

Differs from Stata Stata sums two arcsines; metafor PFT averages them. Multiply yi by 2 and vi by 4 to match Stata scale. No continuity adjustment is needed at zero/all events.

Stata reference · R reference

Unstandardized mean differences

Stata 

meta esize n1 m1 sd1 n0 m0 sd0, esize(mdiff)

R metafor 

metafor::escalc(measure = "MD", m1i = m1, sd1i = sd1, n1i = n1, m2i = m0, sd2i = sd0, n2i = n0, data = data, vtype = "HO")

Differs from Stata vtype="HO" uses the pooled within-group variance, matching Stata esize(mdiff) default equal-variance sampling variance. metafor default vtype="LS" instead uses separate group variances; use it with Stata unequal.

Stata

R metafor 

metafor::escalc(measure = "COR", ri = r, ni = n, data = data)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Correlations must be within (-1,1); sampling variance depends on transformation.

Stata reference · R reference

Meta-regression on centered publication year

Stata 

meta regress c.year

R metafor 

metafor::rma(yi = yi, vi = vi, mods = ~year, data = data, method = "REML")

Differs from Stata Uses year on its original scale, so the intercept refers to year zero as in the Stata command. Assumes the Stata declared model is random(REML); match its model declaration and standard-error options.

Stata reference · R reference

Categorical REML meta-regression

Stata 

meta regress i.x, random(reml)

R metafor 

metafor::rma(yi, vi, mods = ~factor(x), data = data, method = "REML")

Differs from Stata Categorical REML meta-regression with ordinary normal-reference inference. Knapp-Hartung requires Stata se(khartung) and R test="knha", which are not requested here.

Stata reference · R reference

Random-effects meta-regression with moderator

Stata 

meta regress x

R metafor 

metafor::rma(yi = yi, vi = vi, mods = ~x, data = data, method = "REML")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Meta-regression relates study-level summaries, not individual-level effects.

Random-effects pooled inference using z

Stata 

meta summarize, random(reml)

R metafor 

metafor::rma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = data, method = "REML", test = "z")

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Only knha corresponds to a Knapp-Hartung correction; z/t are explicit inference alternatives.

Stata reference · R reference

Prediction interval for a new study's true effect

Stata 

meta summarize, random(reml) predinterval

R metafor 

{ fit <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = data, method = "REML"); out <- stats::predict(fit); half <- stats::qt(.975, df = fit$k - 2) * sqrt(fit$tau2 + fit$se^2); out$pi.lb <- out$pred - half; out$pi.ub <- out$pred + half; out }

Differs from Stata Random-effects REML true-effect prediction interval. The displayed calculation uses Stata t(K-2) and sqrt(tau2+SE(mu)^2); pooled-mean confidence limits retain their normal reference. Require at least three studies.
